issues.legal_issue: A subtenant is not protected from eviction by a notification permitting tenancy transfers incidental to the sale of a business unless the required transfer of the business is established.
material_facts: The original tenant had sublet the premises to the appellant, who claimed an interest in the premises following dissolution of their partnership.
The appellant relied on a notification permitting certain transfers incidental to the sale of a business as a going concern, with its stock-in-trade and goodwill.

There was no evidence that the business had been assigned to the appellant as a going concern with its stock-in-trade and goodwill, or that the tenancy transfer was incidental to such an assignment; the dissolution deed was not before the Court.
The appellant had not raised the business-assignment contention in the High Court or in the special leave petition.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was not entitled to the protection of the notification, and the contention was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 makes subletting, assignment, or transfer of a tenant’s interest unlawful, subject to the proviso empowering the State Government to permit specified transfers by notification. The notification relied on permits a transfer or assignment incidental to the sale of a business as a going concern together with its stock-in-trade and goodwill; the claimant must establish that qualifying business assignment and that the tenancy transfer was incidental to it.

rule.if: appeal_against_eviction and occupant_claims_business_transfer_protection and tenant_sublet_premises and not qualifying_business_assignment_proved

predicates.appeal_against_eviction: The occupant pursued an appeal challenging a decree for eviction.
predicates.occupant_claims_business_transfer_protec: The occupant claimed that a transfer of the tenancy accompanying a business transfer protected the occupant from eviction.
predicates.tenant_sublet_premises: The tenant sublet the premises to the occupant.
predicates.qualifying_business_assignment_proved: The occupant established that the business was assigned as a going concern with its stock and goodwill and that the tenancy transfer was incidental to that assignment.

issues.definition: When an occupant appeals an eviction decree after claiming protection based on a business transfer, the occupant is not protected if the tenant sublet the premises and the occupant did not establish a qualifying business assignment.

issues.legal_issue: Joining an invalid subtenant to a landlord’s eviction suit against the tenant does not convert the suit into a proceeding against a trespasser or remove it from the rent-control court’s jurisdiction.
material_facts: The landlords brought an eviction suit against the appellant and the other occupants, including the original tenant.
The appellant was alleged to occupy the premises under an invalid subtenancy.
The eviction suit was decreed, and the appellant argued that the rent-control court lacked jurisdiction because the suit against him was one against a trespasser.
issues.conclusion: The rent-control court had jurisdiction; joining the appellant as an invalid subtenant did not change the character of the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 28 of the Bombay Rent Act, as explained in Importers and Manufacturers Ltd. v. Pheroz Framroze Taraporewala, joining a subtenant whose subtenancy is invalid does not alter the character of a suit between landlord and tenant or take it outside the Rent Act. Hiralal Vallabhram v. Kastorbhai Lalbhai is distinguishable: there the appellate court ordered eviction of the subtenant alone as a trespasser and made no eviction order against the tenants-in-chief, making the proceeding one between an owner and a trespasser.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_suit: The landlord brought an eviction proceeding under the rent-control regime.
predicates.landlord_seeks_eviction_of_tenant_and_su: The landlord sought eviction of both the tenant and the subtenant in the same proceeding.
predicates.subtenant_is_joined_as_invalid_occupant: The subtenant was joined as an occupant whose subtenancy was invalid.

issues.definition: A rent-control court has jurisdiction when a landlord seeks eviction of the tenant and an invalid subtenant together in a rent-control eviction suit.
